headline: Democrats flip Congress as the U.S.-Iran standoff and Canada's budget dominate the week
summary: Democrats won the U.S. midterms and Trump reshuffled his White House, naming Stephen Miller chief of staff. The U.S.-Iran standoff over Hormuz kept oil prices high, while Canada tabled its budget and lost 4,700 jobs in October.

top.headline: Democrats flip Congress; final House and Senate counts still firming up
top.what: Democrats won control of the House and are projected to hold at least 54 Senate seats; the Alaska and Mississippi Senate races are unresolved and Democrats are now eyeing Trump's tariffs.
top.why: It shifts the balance of power in Washington and could affect tariffs on Canadian goods.

top.headline: U.S.-Iran standoff: more limited strikes, blockade enforcement, talks continue
top.what: The U.S. struck near Qeshm Island and disabled a cargo ship it said was breaching its Iran blockade, while Trump says talks are progressing and Hormuz stays closed.
top.why: Oil near US$107 a barrel feeds into Ontario gas and grocery prices.

top.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff
top.what: Trump replaced Susie Wiles with Miller, an architect of his immigration crackdown, starting Nov. 9.
top.why: It signals a harder line in the White House as it deals with a Democratic Congress and Canada.

top.headline: Carney's second budget projects a $62.3B deficit
top.what: The federal budget projects a $62.3-billion deficit with about $142 billion in new spending, plus updated immigration levels.
top.why: It sets federal spending and taxes that affect Ontario households and businesses.

top.headline: Israel's president taps Eisenkot to form a government
top.what: Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot 28 days to build a coalition after the Oct. 27 election left neither bloc with a majority.
top.why: A change in Israeli leadership could shift regional conflicts that move oil prices.

top.headline: Canada loses 4,700 jobs; unemployment rises to 6.7%
top.what: Statistics Canada reported October job losses and a higher unemployment rate.
top.why: A weaker job market bears on Bank of Canada rate decisions and Ontario workers.

top.headline: Ottawa presses Stelco's owner over Hamilton layoffs
top.what: Ottawa asked the Competition Bureau to probe Stelco's owner as layoffs of up to 500 workers loom after U.S. tariffs.
top.why: Hamilton steel jobs are at stake and the case tests takeover commitments.

top.headline: Ontario students walk out over OSAP cuts
top.what: Thousands of students walked out over cuts to Ontario student grants and the end of the tuition freeze.
top.why: Higher costs for Ontario students and colleges.
